{{nihongo|'''Kanda Shrine'''|神田神社 (東白川村)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mino Province]].

'''Kanda Shrine'''（かんだじんじゃ）is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kando}}, {{ill|Higashishirakawa, Gifu|Q1202765|qid=Q1202765}}, {{ill|Kamo District, Gifu|Q1348656|qid=Q1348656}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|Q131277|qid=Q131277}}. It is regarded as Kanda Shrine listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} for {{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156}} Kamo District.

The annual grand festival in late September includes ritual ceremonies, lion dance, and ceremonial sake distribution. Floats used to be pulled through the village, but this stopped in the 1950s due to depopulation. In {{ill|2008|Q2004|qid=Q2004}}（{{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 20）, a new float was built and the procession revived.

=== Overview ===
It is said to have been founded in {{ill|Yōrō|Q1373061|qid=Q1373061}} 2 ({{ill|718|Q23534|qid=Q23534}}). In the Engishiki period, "Kanda" is said to have been read as "Kamuda." It declined after the mid-Heian period, but was restored in Kakei 2 ({{ill|1388|Q6365|qid=Q6365}}), and through {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}} was renamed '''Hakusan Myōdaigongen'''.

It declined again in the Muromachi period, but was restored in Eiroku 1 ({{ill|1558|Q6601|qid=Q6601}}). Buildings were rebuilt in Kyōhō 2 ({{ill|1717|Q6895|qid=Q6895}}).

In Meiji 1 ({{ill|1868|Q7717|qid=Q7717}}), this area underwent thorough {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|Q702298|qid=Q702298}} under the {{ill|Naegi Domain|Q10863458|qid=Q10863458}}, and Hakusan Myōdaigongen was renamed Kanda Shrine. In Meiji 3 ({{ill|1870|Q7741|qid=Q7741}}), the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Department of Divinities}} recognized it as the Shikinaisha Kanda Shrine. In Meiji 4 ({{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}}) it became a gōsha of Naegi Prefecture, and in Meiji 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}) a gōsha of Gifu Prefecture.

On July 1, 1952 (Shōwa 27), it was designated by Gifu Prefectural Shrine Office as a shrine receiving regular offerings (Kinpei-sha designation No. 13){{sfn|木村|1997|p=121}}.
